flagged.evidence: The item defines the neighbourhood category as the full subcategory of Open(X), while def-open-set-category-topological-space says its arrows are "V \to U when V \subseteq U". It then calls \(\mathcal F_x=\varinjlim_{x\in U}\mathcal F(U)\) a filtered colimit. But def-presheaf-on-topological-space makes \(\mathcal F\) contravariant, so its restriction is a diagram \(\mathcal N_x^{op}\to\mathbf{Set}\), not a diagram on the displayed full subcategory \(\mathcal N_x\). The cited filtered-colimit definition requires a diagram \(D:\mathcal J\to\mathbf{Set}\). Thus the stated category does not type the asserted colimit; the index must be explicitly reversed.

[F2] cites def-germ-of-section for "(\varphi_U(s))_x=\varphi_x(s_x)". That dependency defines only germs and the canonical map \(\mathcal F(U)\to\mathcal F_x\), and says "If \(V\subseteq U\) also contains \(x\), then \((s|_V)_x=s_x\)"; it never defines the induced map \(\varphi_x\) or proves its compatibility with germs. The cited item therefore does not license [F2].

Step 3.1 calls \(\{B_x:x\in U_\alpha\}\) "the basis cover of \(U_\alpha\)", but step 1.2 only chose \(B_x\subseteq U_{\alpha(x)}\), not \(B_x\subseteq U_\alpha\). If \(x\in U_\alpha\cap U_\beta\) and \(\alpha(x)=\beta\), the selected \(B_x\) may extend outside \(U_\alpha\). Hence this family need not be a cover by basis elements of \(U_\alpha\), so the assumed basis condition cannot yet be applied. Refining by basis elements inside \(B_x\cap U_\alpha\) repairs the gap.

The page says the germ examples show "why one point never determines a section". For the one-point space \(X=\{x\}\), the only open neighbourhood of \(x\) is \(X\), so for any sheaf \(\mathcal F\) the stalk \(\mathcal F_x\) is canonically \(\mathcal F(X)\); the germ at \(x\) does determine the global section. The intended claim is only that one stalk does not determine a section in general.

[F2] cites def-germ-of-section for "Germs commute with morphisms of presheaves: \((\varphi_U(s))_x=\varphi_x(s_x)\)". That dependency defines a germ and restriction invariance only; it contains no morphism \(\varphi\), induced stalk map \(\varphi_x\), or compatibility statement. It does not support the cited assertion.

After obtaining \(s_x=s'_x\) for every \(x\), step 4.1 says "and then [L1] gives \(s=s'\)". But [L1], lem-morphisms-of-sheaves-determined-by-stalks, concerns equality of two morphisms of sheaves from equality of their stalk maps; \(s,s'\) are sections, not morphisms or stalk maps. Equality follows instead by choosing local neighbourhoods from the germ equalities and applying sheaf locality, so the written inference is unsupported but immediately repairable.
